title: Decision rights in the GTA AI documents
scope: Built only from the seven documents in the project. Roles are quoted as written and are not mapped to named people.

status_values.not_named: A decision or approval is required or offered, and no provision names who makes it.

Artificial Intelligence Responsible Use (SS-23-002), 6. Data Protection, Safety and Privacy, p.9
Generative AI Guidelines for Responsible Use (GS-25-001), Mitigating the Risks of Generative AI: Rubric, p.10

roles.citation: Generative AI Guidelines for Responsible Use (GS-25-001), Guidelines > Use AI Tools Safely and Properly, p.2

decisions.status_note: Three provisions name three different approvers. No document gives a request process.

decisions.status_note: The role is named but not identified; the documents do not say who holds it in an agency.

Enterprise Artificial Intelligence Responsible Use (PS-23-001), Policy, p.3

roles.citation: Artificial Intelligence Responsible Use (SS-23-002), 3. Procuring AI Solutions, p.5

channel.as_written: Business Solutions Review (BSR) Request form to GTA via email

roles.citation: Generative AI Responsible Use (SS-25-001), Standard (opening paragraphs, before section 1), p.2

decisions.status_note: Agencies 'retain discretion'. How this fits with GTA's advance approval of any GenAI procurement (DR-03) is not stated.

Generative AI Responsible Use (SS-25-001), Standard (opening paragraphs, before section 1), p.2

roles.citation: Generative AI Responsible Use (SS-25-001), 3.0 Common Gen AI Use Cases (sentence below the table), p.8

decisions.status_note: The provision gives where to send the request. It does not say who grants it, or which uses need it.

decisions.decision: Reviewing AI-generated content before it is used

Artificial Intelligence Responsible Use (SS-23-002), 5. Ensuring Accuracy and Appropriateness of AI-generated Outputs, p.9

decisions.status_note: SS-25-001 defines Qualified Personnel as the subject-matter employee who would otherwise be responsible for the content; SS-23-002 names the business owner or designated personnel, and a different trigger.

timing_as_written.as_written: before being used in any official capacity

Generative AI Guidelines for Responsible Use (GS-25-001), Guidelines > Use AI Tools Safely and Properly, p.2

Artificial Intelligence Responsible Use (SS-23-002), 8. Reporting Misuse, p.11

excluded: Reporting duties (incidents, misuse, development risks, inventories) are routes for information, not decisions; see next_steps_scan.md.
The guiding-principle items and GS-25-002 name no decider for any step.
Roles, bodies and documents outside the seven documents (for example SM-14-008, the State CTO, EPMO, DOAS, OPB, an Executive Decision-Making Board) are not included.
